steps.label: Read the functionality and leakage contract

cards.title: Useful features, exact encrypted replay
cards.body: A selected public semantic fixture completed 384 Learn events, 96 Infer events and 256 exact-original expiries through BFV and an independently verifying durable receiver. One shared-machine run took 219.733 seconds.
cards.limit: The receiver retains the full BFV key. This selected subset has 28/32 correct final labels; exact arithmetic does not make every semantic answer correct.

cards.title: A useful, deliberately small semantic learner
cards.body: A frozen SmolLM3 factual scorer feeds a four-bin recency learner. Original features score 51.0010% on the same fresh synthetic text/history study. All eleven preregistered gates passed.
cards.limit: A trusted plaintext issuer supplies the abstraction. The study is local and synthetic, with repeated texts across histories. Spanning exact-score credentials reveal its small aggregate image.

cards.title: A complete designated-recipient workload
cards.body: The original fixed-span workload completed with all 96 integer comparisons passing. Public processing, independent replay and service shutdown precede private decoding. Public work took 11,697.338 seconds (3h 14m 57s).
cards.limit: Classical DDH, a known public fixture, honest setup/erasure and shared-account processes. Recipient credentials still read their full fixed per-input query span outside the journal. Final label accuracy remains 18/32.

cards.title: Public-coin setup joins the durable journal
cards.body: The honest public constructor generates no scalar master. Its journal join completed all 44 independent transition replays; both ordered histories agree and all four private integers match the fixture. Reopening and exact historical retries preserve the head.
cards.limit: Honest sampling and independent recipient registration remain premises. Recipients retain the full per-input fixed span, including expired inputs. The setup proof excludes the instrumented timing view; this arithmetic fixture establishes no model utility or whole-protocol privacy.

cards.title: A generic runtime for Lean-emitted updates
cards.body: A Rust TFHE interpreter executes the Lean-emitted Boolean schedules. Both encrypted updates and sign answers match the integer oracle; all four separate-process byte comparisons pass. Independent plaintext checks cover 25,600 Learn rows and 49,152 Infer rows.
cards.limit: These are finite checks. The unrestricted reader key remains. The separate formal proposal does not prove Rust parsing, TFHE correctness or universal byte determinism. The older long-run failure remains part of the record.

cards.title: A longer replay stops at Learn 14
cards.body: The first thirteen Learn replay pairs match; the fourteenth produces different ciphertext bytes from identical public inputs. A separate emitted runtime with a fixed FFT plan later passes five preregistered replay pairs, including that public input case.
cards.limit: Byte mismatch does not imply incorrect plaintext. The five controls are independent cases, not a completed learning trajectory; no new plaintext decoding was done. They establish neither the old cause nor general deterministic replay.

cards.title: A checked collection of formal ingredients
cards.body: The combined proposal passed its overlay build, four umbrellas, patch application and import boundaries. It joins signed-word arithmetic, Lean-emitted learner schedules, adaptation dynamics and full unique decoding over existing Reed–Solomon objects.
cards.limit: A checked proposal patch, not a landed companion change. Existing dependency oleans were reused. No clean whole-tree build or universal Rust refinement is inferred.

cards.title: A security number needs its assumptions
cards.body: The current verdict ledger distinguishes unique-decoding, idealised Johnson and legacy capacity accounting. The withdrawn capacity figure must not be presented as the system’s security level.
cards.limit: This is a guide to the repository’s current verdicts, not a fresh protocol audit. Query accounting and commit-phase error must not silently become a whole-system claim.

cards.title: Private continuation with a fixed horizon
cards.body: Independent functional-encryption instances are set up backwards, so each transition embeds an already existing future public key. The argument retains the whole future key package in the adversary’s view.
cards.limit: A classical, selective-state construction direction under explicit primitive assumptions and honest erasure. Public commands, copying and authorized branches remain. The symbolic witness does not implement encryption.

cards.title: A private resident needs restricted read authority
cards.body: The target releases only the authorized answer while preserving reusable protected state. A journal can regulate a published history; surviving keys may still read inputs or support local counterfactual computations.
cards.limit: Successful encrypted arithmetic, durable integrity and useful adaptation are separate properties. Their current demonstrations do not establish full mental autarky under the declared exposure game.

cards.title: A conditional post-quantum route, with costs
cards.metric_label: finite sizing is not a security level
cards.body: Independent review accepts a conditional fixed-policy LWE construction. A narrower QPT argument permits smaller widths. One n = 1,024 sizing example still needs 84.43 MB per ciphertext and 86.46 GB of public matrices; these are calculated, packed sizes, not generated objects.
cards.limit: The example normalizes unresolved source constants. Gaussian implementation error, reduction errors and computational hardness remain open. Fixed per-input recipient leakage persists, and receipt composition is separate. No whole-resident post-quantum result is claimed.
